questionBank.chapterTitle: Airplane Flying Handbook (FAA-H-8083-3C) Chapter 18: Emergency Procedures Introduction

question: What are key considerations for executing an emergency landing in small fixed-wing airplanes?

correct_answers.text: Use airplane structure for self-protection
Consider almost any terrain as suitable
Protect passengers using airplane structure

source: Airplane Flying Handbook (FAA-H-8083-3C) Chapter 18: Emergency Procedures Introduction

question: Which of the following are TRUE regarding the types of emergency landings defined in the Airplane Flying Handbook?

correct_answers.text: A precautionary landing is generally less hazardous than a forced landing because the pilot has more time for terrain selection and approach planning
Ditching is defined as a forced or precautionary landing on water
A forced landing is an immediate landing necessitated by the inability to continue further flight

wrong_answers.text: A precautionary landing requires the pilot to land immediately due to complete engine failure
Ditching refers exclusively to a forced landing on water, not a precautionary landing on water
A forced landing is always planned in advance, allowing the pilot time to select suitable terrain
A precautionary landing is more hazardous than a forced landing because the pilot cannot use engine power
Fuel shortage alone is never a valid reason to initiate a precautionary landing
A non-instrument-rated pilot trapped by weather should always continue flight rather than consider a precautionary landing
Wishful thinking is an acceptable decision-making strategy when facing a self-inflicted predicament in flight
During a precautionary landing, the pilot cannot use power to compensate for errors in judgment or technique

source: AFH Chapter 18, Section 18.2: Types of Emergency Landings

question: Which of the following are common errors a pilot might make due to an undue desire to save the airplane during an emergency?

correct_answers.text: Making a 180° turn back to the runway when available altitude is insufficient.
Stretching the glide without regard for minimum control speed.
Accepting an approach and touchdown situation that leaves no margin for error.

wrong_answers.text: Failure to lower the nose to maintain flying speed.
Delay in the selection of the most suitable landing area.
Desperate attempts to correct whatever went wrong at the expense of airplane control.
Prioritizing occupant safety by sacrificing the airplane.
Maintaining composure and applying general emergency procedures.
Immediately securing the engine after a power loss.

question: What are key considerations for a pilot during an emergency landing to minimize crash injuries?

correct_answers.text: Keeping the cabin area intact

Avoiding forceful bodily contact with interior structure

wrong_answers.text: Using essential structure for slowing down

correct_answers.text: An excessive nose-low pitch attitude risks 'sticking' the nose in the ground on flat terrain

wrong_answers.text: Maintaining a wings-level attitude throughout the approach is the primary cause of emergency landing fatalities

correct_answers.text: Prioritizing positive airplane control over configuration and checklist tasks during the final approach.

wrong_answers.text: Always performing a gear-up landing on any terrain to minimize damage.
Fully extending flaps during an emergency approach to maximize lift.

Dimensions and slope of the chosen field

question: When executing a water ditching or snow landing, which of the following procedures are recommended?

wrong_answers.text: Extend flaps fully to maximize drag and reduce touchdown speed
Lower retractable gear to provide a stable platform on the water surface
Approach at a steep angle to ensure positive contact with the water surface

question: According to the Airplane Flying Handbook, what are key considerations and initial actions during an emergency descent?

correct_answers.text: Reduce power to idle and place the propeller control in the low pitch (high rpm) position, if equipped.
Establish a bank of approximately 30 to 45° to maintain positive load factors.
Extend landing gear and flaps as recommended by the manufacturer for maximum drag.

wrong_answers.text: Maintain cruise power to ensure adequate control authority.
Place the propeller control in the high pitch (low rpm) position to reduce drag.
Avoid extending landing gear or flaps to prevent structural stress.
Initiate the descent in a straight line to reach the ground faster.
Exceed the never-exceed speed (VNE) if necessary to achieve the fastest descent rate.
Increase airspeed beyond the maximum flap extended speed (VFE) for maximum effectiveness.
Maintain a wings-level attitude to minimize G forces.
Avoid making a radio call to prevent distracting other aircraft.

source: Airplane Flying Handbook (FAA-H-8083-3C) Chapter 18: Emergency Procedures Introduction

question: Based on the provided text, what are valid reasons for initiating an emergency descent and important speed considerations during the maneuver?

correct_answers.text: A sudden loss of cabin pressurization.
The objective is to descend as rapidly as possible without exceeding structural limitations.
Comply with the design maneuvering speed (VA) limitations if the descent is conducted in turbulent conditions.

wrong_answers.text: To practice high-speed maneuvers for proficiency.
To intentionally exceed the maximum landing gear extended speed (VLE) for a quicker descent.
To cool the engine cylinders during prolonged flight.
The primary goal is to maintain a constant airspeed throughout the descent.
To test the aircraft's structural limits.
To avoid making a precautionary landing.
To achieve the slowest possible rate of descent to conserve fuel.

source: Airplane Flying Handbook (FAA-H-8083-3C) Chapter 18: Emergency Procedures Introduction

correct_answers.text: In-flight engine fires

question: What are the initial steps a pilot should take upon discovering an in-flight engine compartment fire, unless the AFM/POH directs otherwise?

correct_answers.text: Place the mixture control in the idle cut off position

wrong_answers.text: Immediately shut off the ignition switch to prevent sparks
Increase airspeed to blow out the flames
Activate the fire suppression system before adjusting fuel controls
Turn the electrical master switch off as the first action
Open the throttle fully to consume remaining fuel faster
Declare an emergency and land before adjusting any controls
Place the fuel selector to the richest mixture setting
Feather the propeller as the very first corrective action

source: AFH Chapter 18, Section 18.15 – Engine Fire

question: How can a pilot distinguish an oil-fed engine compartment fire from a fuel-fed engine compartment fire, and what action addresses an oil-fed fire?

correct_answers.text: An oil-fed fire produces thick black smoke, while a fuel-fed fire produces bright orange flames
Stopping propeller rotation halts the engine-driven oil pump feeding an oil-fed fire

wrong_answers.text: A fuel-fed fire produces thick black smoke, while an oil-fed fire produces bright orange flames

source: AFH Chapter 18, Section 18.15 – Engine Fire

correct_answers.text: Shutting off the electrical master switch prevents use of panel radios for transmitting distress messages

wrong_answers.text: The electrical master switch should always be the first item shut off during any engine fire
